title: Best Time to Visit Masai Mara for the Great Migration
metaTitle: Best Time to Visit Masai Mara for Migration 2026
metaDescription: Which is the best time to visit Masai Mara? This 2026 guide covers the Great Migration months, calving season, low season, and the single best answer for first-time and repeat visitors.
keywords: best time to visit Masai Mara

appendFaqs.question: Which is the best time to visit Masai Mara?
appendFaqs.answer: The single best time to visit the Masai Mara is during the Great Migration, between July and October, with August and September being the peak months for the dramatic Mara River crossings. During this period, more than 1.5 million wildebeest and several hundred thousand zebras and gazelles cross the Mara River from the Serengeti, attracting large predators and offering some of the most dramatic wildlife viewing on earth. For travelers who want a quieter, greener, and more affordable trip, the shoulder months of late June and early November offer excellent wildlife viewing with fewer visitors.

appendFaqs.question: When to visit Masai Mara for calving season?
appendFaqs.answer: The calving season in the Masai Mara runs from January to March, with the peak in February. During this period, more than 500,000 wildebeest calves are born on the southern plains of the Serengeti, attracting large numbers of predators and offering extraordinary predator-prey interactions. The calving season is less crowded than the migration crossings, the prices are lower, and the resident game in the Mara remains excellent year-round.

appendFaqs.question: When do the wildebeest migrate through the Mara?
appendFaqs.answer: The wildebeest migration enters the Masai Mara from the Serengeti between July and August, depending on rainfall and grass conditions. The herds stay in the Mara through October, gradually moving south as the rains begin. The Mara River crossings — the most dramatic moments of the migration — typically occur between late July and early October, with peak crossing activity in August and September.

appendFaqs.question: What is the best time to visit Masai Mara on a budget?
appendFaqs.answer: The best budget months to visit the Masai Mara are the long rains (April to May) and the short rains (November), when lodge rates are 20 to 40 percent lower than the peak season. Wildlife viewing remains excellent during these months, with the calving season in January to March, the migration in July to October, and the resident game year-round. The shoulder months of late June and early November offer a good balance of price and wildlife.

title: Serengeti vs Masai Mara: Which Safari Destination is Right for You?
metaTitle: Serengeti vs Masai Mara Safari Comparison 2026
metaDescription: Which is better, Serengeti or Masai Mara? This 2026 comparison covers wildlife, accessibility, cost, and the best time to visit, with a clear recommendation for every type of traveler.
keywords: which is better Serengeti or Masai Mara
is Serengeti better than Masai Mara

appendFaqs.question: Which is better, Serengeti or Masai Mara?
appendFaqs.answer: The honest answer is that neither is 'better' — they are different ecosystems that offer different experiences. The Serengeti is much larger (14,750 vs 1,510 square kilometers), more remote, and offers a more expansive, less-crowded safari. The Masai Mara has higher wildlife density, easier access from Nairobi, more reliable river crossings, and a more developed tourism infrastructure. Most experienced safari travelers visit both, often on a single 10- to 14-day Kenya-Tanzania combination.

appendFaqs.question: Is Serengeti better than Masai Mara?
appendFaqs.answer: The Serengeti is 'better' for travelers who want a more remote, less-crowded, more expansive safari with a wider variety of landscapes (plains, kopjes, riverine forests, woodlands). The Serengeti is also slightly cheaper for the same lodge standard, and the Serengeti-to-Ngorongoro add-on is one of the most dramatic safari extensions in Africa. The Masai Mara is 'better' for travelers who want easier access, more reliable big cat sightings, the most dramatic river crossings, and a more developed tourism infrastructure. The right choice depends on your priorities.

appendFaqs.question: Is the Serengeti in Tanzania or Kenya?
appendFaqs.answer: The Serengeti National Park is in northern Tanzania, bordering the Masai Mara National Reserve in southern Kenya. The two parks form one continuous ecosystem, separated by an international border that the migrating wildebeest cross twice a year. From the wildlife's perspective, the Serengeti and the Masai Mara are a single ecosystem; from the traveler's perspective, they are two separate parks in two separate countries with different visa requirements, different currencies, and different tourism infrastructure.

appendFaqs.question: Which one is closer to Nairobi?
appendFaqs.answer: The Masai Mara is much closer to Nairobi than the Serengeti. The Mara is a 5- to 6-hour drive or a 45-minute flight from Nairobi. The Serengeti requires a flight to Kilimanjaro or Arusha (about 1 hour), then a connecting flight to a Serengeti airstrip (about 1.5 hours), then a short transfer to the lodge. The Mara is the right choice for a short safari (3-5 days); the Serengeti is better for a longer safari (5-10 days) or a combined Kenya-Tanzania itinerary.

appendFaqs.question: Which is cheaper, Serengeti or Masai Mara?
appendFaqs.answer: Tanzania, including the Serengeti, is generally 10 to 20 percent cheaper than Kenya for the same lodge standard, because park fees and accommodation rates are slightly lower. A 5-day mid-range Serengeti safari in 2026 costs about $3,500 to $5,500 per person; a 5-day mid-range Masai Mara safari costs about $3,500 to $5,000 per person. The difference is small, and the choice usually comes down to the wildlife and the experience rather than the price.

appendFaqs.question: Should I visit both Serengeti and Masai Mara?
appendFaqs.answer: If you have at least 10 days and a budget of $8,000 to $12,000 per person for a mid-range experience, visiting both is the most rewarding East Africa safari option. A 10- to 14-day Mara-Serengeti-Ngorongoro combination covers the most iconic wildlife in East Africa, with the migration, the Big Five, the Ngorongoro Crater, and a wide range of landscapes. The logistics are straightforward: a light aircraft connects the Mara to the Serengeti in about 90 minutes, and most safari operators handle the cross-border logistics seamlessly.
